count_frames.description: Decode the whole video stream to count frames exactly. This is the only way to know the true end, but it costs a full pass. Turn it off for very long files and rely on stream metadata instead.
count_frames.title: Count Frames

probe_seek.description: Actually attempt a frame extraction at the container's reported end. This is what turns a metadata comparison into a reproduction of the bug, so leave it on unless you only want the numbers.
probe_seek.title: Probe Seek

duration_seconds.description: Duration this stream declares, if it declares one.
duration_seconds.title: Duration Seconds

container_duration_seconds.description: Duration the container declares. Usually the longest stream.
container_duration_seconds.title: Container Duration Seconds

streams.description: Every stream and the duration it claims.
streams.title: Streams

decoded_frame_count.description: Video frames actually decoded. Null if count_frames was off.
decoded_frame_count.title: Decoded Frame Count

frames_imply_seconds.description: decoded_frame_count / frame_rate -- duration the frames imply.
frames_imply_seconds.title: Frames Imply Seconds

drift_seconds.description: container_duration - video_duration. Positive means the file claims to run longer than its video does, which is the dangerous direction.
drift_seconds.title: Drift Seconds

last_decodable_frame_seconds.description: Timestamp of the last frame that could actually be decoded.
last_decodable_frame_seconds.title: Last Decodable Frame Seconds

seek_at_container_end_fails.description: Tested, not predicted: did extracting a frame just inside the container's reported end actually fail?
seek_at_container_end_fails.title: Seek At Container End Fails

safe.description: True when the drift is negligible and the end-of-file seek worked.
safe.title: Safe

verdict.description: One line on what was found.
verdict.title: Verdict

recommendation.description: How a downstream tool should seek the end of this file.
recommendation.title: Recommendation
